clue.text: National Insurance payment returned to source

indicators.note: returned means the whole run of pieces is sent back the other way, read from the end

parts.note: NI is the standard abbreviation for National Insurance, the UK social security contribution
a giro is a payment made by bank transfer, or a British state benefit cheque

explanation.surface: A National Insurance payment bounced back to wherever it came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NIGIRO round as a whole. A giro is a British bank-transfer payment, once also the name of a benefit cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: the origin of something is its source or starting point.

clue.text: Riotous mob in America could be from Clapham

indicators.note: riotous suggests wild disorder, so the letters of mob in are thrown into a new order

parts.note: US is the usual abbreviation for the United States, i.e. America

explanation.surface: A rioting mob in the USA might have come from a South London district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riotous' shuffles the letters to OMNIB. 'The man on the Clapham omnibus' is the classic English legal figure of the ordinary reasonable person; Clapham is a district of South London.
explanation.definitionFit: Allusion: the phrase 'the man on the Clapham omnibus' makes this vehicle what such a person could be riding from Clapham.

clue.text: Neutral role I held in Lima after reconstruction

indicators.note: held in says the role-and-I pair is gripped inside the rearranged city's letters
after reconstruction means the letters of Lima have been rebuilt in a different order

parts.note: a part is a role played by an actor

explanation.surface: An unbiased part played by someone in the Peruvian capital once it was rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after reconstruction' rearranges the city to IMAL, and 'held in' splits it around the role-and-I pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a neutral person takes no side, which is being impartial or unbiased.

clue.text: Hopes for the French uprising during the 15th March say

indicators.note: during says one piece falls within the span of the other, so it sits inside

parts.note: the Ides of March fall on the 15th; 'say' marks it as one example, since other months have Ides too

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the word goes upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: la is a French word for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: Hopes for a French revolt around the date Caesar was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns the French article round, and 'during' sets it inside. The Roman Ides fell on the 15th of March, May, July and October, hence 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Near-synonyms: ideals are the hoped-for standards or aims one aspires to.

clue.text: Joint committee dumped after losing direction

indicators.note: losing means one letter is taken away from the word for dumped

parts.note: binned means thrown in the bin, dumped
N for north is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A joint committee scrapped after it lost its way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' drops one N from the word for dumped; 'Joint' is an adjective here, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: something joint is shared or put together by several parties, as in a combined effort.

clue.text: Skip over part of debt I'm owing

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the run is turned upside down, read from the bottom
part of says the letters are a stretch lifted from inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Skipping over some of what I owe in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of' takes TIMO from 'debT I'M Owing' and 'over' turns it round. 'Skip over' looks like one phrase, but 'over' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to skip something is to leave it out or pass it by.

clue.text: Show of resentment at criminal possibly coming before dinner

parts.note: a criminal is one example of a bad person, so bad describes such a wrongdoer
grace is the prayer said before a meal

explanation.surface: Someone sulks at a crook who might turn up just ahead of the evening meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: doing something with bad grace means showing unwillingness or resentment.

clue.text: Comes close to treason not to get involved

indicators.note: get involved suggests the letters becoming tangled together, rearranged after the two named ones are taken out

explanation.surface: Someone edges near to betrayal while trying to stay out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to' removes T and O from TREASON, leaving REASN, and 'get involved' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to approach or draw near is to come close to something.

clue.text: Deceived that flooding cut off half of Dedham

indicators.note: cut off means the word for flooding is truncated, its tail removed

parts.note: a deluge is a great flood

indicators.note: half of says only the first half of the place name is used

explanation.surface: Misled about how floods isolated half of an English village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut off' trims GE from DELUGE to give DELU, and 'half of' takes DED from Dedham, a village on the Essex-Suffolk border.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone deluded has been misled or fooled into a false belief.

clue.text: Relative is extremely nice — that's a relief

indicators.note: extremely points at the extremities of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: phew is the exclamation made when relieved

explanation.surface: A very kind relation, which is a relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters N and E of 'nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sister's or brother's son is a family member, a relation.

clue.text: Idle talk leads to drop in unearned income

parts.note: wind is empty talk, hot air
a fall is a drop

explanation.surface: Gossip triggers a fall in passive income.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a windfall is an unexpected gain, money that comes without effort.

clue.text: Campaign for South Africa to invest in oil

indicators.note: to invest in means to put something into, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: crude is unrefined oil

explanation.surface: A drive for South Africa to put money into the oil industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to invest in' reads as finance, but it signals putting one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a crusade is a vigorous campaign for a cause.

clue.text: To forget about resistance by early gladiators is a crime

indicators.note: about says the word for forgetting wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: to bury something, as in burying the hatchet, is to put it away and forget it
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
the early part of the word gladiators is its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Ignoring the resistance put up by the first gladiators is a criminal act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the forgetting word around the rest; 'early gladiators' supplies the first three letters, a looser take than the usual single initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: breaking into a building to steal is a specific crime, housebreaking.

clue.text: Forced Polish leader to stand up against Germany

indicators.note: leader picks out the leading, first letter of the word

parts.note: to rise is to stand up
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A Polish leader was made to stand up against Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish leader' looks like a politician, but it is just the first letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: prised open means levered or forced open.

clue.text: Ready in France to do away with make believe

parts.note: prêt is French for ready
to end something is to do away with it

explanation.surface: Prepared in France to get rid of fantasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to pretend is to act as if something were true, to make believe.

clue.text: Announced ending of pensions relief

indicators.note: ending of takes just the final letter of the following word

parts.note: aid is relief, help given to those in need

explanation.surface: An announcement that pension relief is to end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending of' gives S, the last letter of 'pensions'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something announced has been stated or declared aloud.

clue.text: Banished Castro dies in revolution

indicators.note: in revolution means the letters are turned over and churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A Cuban leader exiled after dying in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in revolution' rearranges CASTRODIES; the Cuban-revolution surface hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone ostracised is shut out or excluded from society, effectively banished.

clue.text: Give up second car I crashed following freeze

indicators.note: a crashed car is wrecked, so its letters with I are scrambled

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for following, as in page references
to ice is to freeze

explanation.surface: Abandon a second car I smashed after an icy spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' looks like an order signal but is the abbreviation F; 'crashed' rearranges the car and I to ACRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to sacrifice something is to surrender or give it up for something else.

clue.text: Bogus husband almost captured tourist's heart

indicators.note: captured means one piece is held inside another
almost means the word is not quite complete, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a husband is a spouse
the heart of the word tourist is its central three letters

explanation.surface: A fake husband nearly took a visitor's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of the word for husband, and 'captured' holds the middle three letters of 'tourist' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something spurious is false or fake, not genuine.

clue.text: Allow collapse of engagement after I'd returned cut stone

indicators.note: after says the engagement piece follows the others
returned says the two letters are sent back the other way

parts.note: I'd is written ID without the apostrophe

indicators.note: cut means the word for stone loses its last letter

parts.note: lapis is Latin for stone, as in lapis lazuli
a date is an engagement, an appointment

explanation.surface: Letting an engagement fall apart after I'd returned a broken gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns I'd round to DI, 'cut' trims the Latin stone, and 'after' puts the engagement last. Lapis lazuli is a blue stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to dilapidate a building is to let it fall into ruin through neglect.

clue.text: Drop girl with disfigurement on back of head

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
a scar is a disfigurement

indicators.note: back of takes the rear, final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A girl drops something with a scar on the back of her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives D, the last letter of 'head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to discard something is to get rid of it, let it go.

clue.text: Cheat by switching over computers

indicators.note: switching over says the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: Macs are Apple computers

explanation.surface: Cheating by changing computer brands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching over' turns MACS around.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a scam is a fraud or swindle, a cheat.

clue.text: Wonderful gift-givers take the leading part in calamities

parts.note: the Magi are the three wise men who brought gifts to the infant Jesus
the leading part of the word calamities is its first three letters

explanation.surface: Splendid present-bringers star in disasters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something magical is enchanting, wonderful.

clue.text: How old a mother is leads to harm

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
age says how old something is

explanation.surface: A mother's age leads to hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'How old a mother is' reads in reverse order: the mother (DAM) comes first, then her age.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: damage is injury or harm.

clue.text: Rush about in drug-free county

indicators.note: in says the letter for about is placed inside the trimmed county
drug-free means without the letter standing for the drug

parts.note: Surrey is an English county south of London
E is short for ecstasy
c, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A dash around an English county free of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' removes the E (ecstasy) from the county, which lies just south of London, and 'in' places C (circa) inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to scurry is to move hurriedly with short quick steps, to rush.

clue.text: Loose relative goes topless

indicators.note: goes topless means the word loses its first letter, its top in a down clue

parts.note: an auntie is a relative

explanation.surface: An unrestrained relation strips off her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes topless' removes the A from AUNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to loose something is to set it free, unfasten it.

clue.text: Massaging is demanding we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: needing means requiring, demanding

explanation.surface: A massage proves exacting work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: kneading muscles is working them with the hands, as in massage.

clue.text: Silver ring gets leading geologist highly excited

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: leading picks out the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A silver ring thrills a leading rock expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' gives G from 'geologist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: agog means eagerly expectant, very excited.

clue.text: Despite being firm about ending of fatwah, a Liberal comes first

indicators.note: comes first says the a-and-Liberal pair stands at the front
about says the word for firm goes round the other letter

parts.note: tough means firm, hard

indicators.note: ending of takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Liberal stays firm on a religious ruling and takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending of' gives H from 'fatwah', 'about' puts TOUGH round it as THOUGH, and 'comes first' places A and L at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: despite and although both concede a point, in spite of that.

clue.text: Lunatic starts to manufacture nightmarish accusations

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening of each word, here the first two letters of each

explanation.surface: A madman begins inventing dreadful charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first two letters of each of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a maniac is a madman, a lunatic.

clue.text: Profound myopia is a sign of great weariness

parts.note: profound means deep
myopia is short sight, read here as the word sight made short, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Severe short-sightedness is a mark of great tiredness.
explanation.walkthrough: Myopia is short sight; read literally, 'short sight' is SIGHT shortened by one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a long heavy exhalation is a classic signal of exhaustion or despair.

clue.text: Ring again to cancel

definitions.meaning: to revoke or annul a law

explanation.surface: Phone back to call something off.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: re-pealing bells means ringing them again, and abolishing a law is revoking it.
